# A1: art and vista pass

Owner: Opus 5.5 high, branch `t3/57671609` (worktree `t3-57671609`). Base: `a09968b` (plus coordinator docs `4c3c681`). R1 candidate `44099bf`; R2 changes are in the section below. Not pushed, no PR.

## Outcome
Floors no longer read as stripes. Caustics read as patchy light. Each priority area has a composed vista, and scatter grows in colonies of varied silhouettes. Presentation only: no file under `src/sim`, `src/content`, `src/save`, `src/ui`, `runtime/app.ts` or `render/expedition.ts` changed. Terrain bytes are identical: all 220 manifest entries match the before bake, and `bake-terrain --verify` passes 220/220.

## What changed
- **Ground and caustics** (`render/materials.ts`).
  - Removed: the global `sin` ripple, which striped every alpha-0 surface (including the legacy island's dry slopes), and the `sin·sin` caustic net.
  - New ground response, built from world-space value noise:
    - soft tonal patches everywhere;
    - wave ripples only on flat, submerged, shallow sediment, in two headings with patchy coverage, fading with depth and distance;
    - current drifts at Basin depths (110–380 m) and speckle below about 300 m;
    - irregular strata on steep ground;
    - fine aperiodic grain near the camera.
  - New caustics: two drifting cell networks, warped by noise and gated by slow light pools. They scale with the lit colour and resolve to their average at distance, and they are skipped below 70 m.
  - Per biome: the response is keyed on depth, slope and wetness. Each region keeps its baked palette, with no bake change. Reef and isles get ripples and caustics, Canopy gets faint ripples, the Basin gets drifts, and the deep gets speckle.
- **Frustum and prism caps** (`biomes/recipe.ts`). Caps faced inward, which is why cups rendered as dark "mushrooms".
- **Scatter** (`biomes/templates.ts`, `biomes/scatter.ts`).
  - 17 new template silhouettes:
    - fans: whip, twin and ruffle, in both the pale and coral fans;
    - slabs: stack, split and wedge;
    - boulders: flat and pair;
    - columns: lean and stump;
    - one shard spray, organ and ring tubes, and a tiered cup.
  - `variants` choose among silhouettes with a slow noise, so neighbours share a form.
  - `clump` seeds colonies on a world lattice, so a colony stays whole across chunk edges, with its largest members at the heart.
  - Instances total 67.5k against 62.7k before. Building every chunk's scatter takes 1.25 s against 1.52 s before, with no sliced step over 2 ms.
  - The keep-out index gained headroom: `blocked(…, bottom)`. Scatter's behaviour is unchanged.
- **Vistas** (new `biomes/vistas.ts`, built by `s2.scatter` into the chunk holding each part's anchor; it follows the floor and yields between parts).
  - **Wreck ridge:** a capsized hull lying on the west flank (ribs rise along the slope normal), a broken bow with a lit beacon over the crest, a fallen boom and debris trails.
  - **Hearth drop:** a coral-crusted arch over the descent (at least 16 m above the passage), kelp and coral on the lip, and bulb clusters down the walls.
  - **Meridian deep works:** an open gantry over the block, framing lattice masts, pipe runs and a lamp avenue to the hatch. The block itself (`structures.ts`) gains pilasters, a hazard plinth and lit windows within the 1.3 m collider trim.
  - **Escarpment:** warm markers on the ledge's outer edge, a survey mast and a broken Meridian ring at the wall's foot.
- **Legacy Basin works** (`ecology.ts`, `basinWorksYard`). Its owner is `expedition.ts`, so the yard is dressed from the region's ecology pass:
  - lamps on the pad's back corners and a lit 50 m mast that rises above the wall;
  - a feed pipe down to the dish spine;
  - a lamp line along the fracture lip, and tube colonies.

## Checks
- `npm test`: 735/735. Heavy (`heavy-check.sh --deadline 1500 npm run test:heavy`): 16/16 files, every one under its memory budget. `npm run build` passes (the bake is re-hashed because `recipe.ts` changed; bytes are unchanged). `bake-terrain --verify`: 220/220.
- New `tests/vistas.test.ts` samples every vista triangle at 1 m or finer against the scatter keep-out: passages with craft height plus 4 m, rescue tethers, mooring pads and structures. It also checks determinism, finite values, cel alpha and LOD. Negative control: a point on the wreck route is blocked; 30 m above it is not.
- **Adverse case found and fixed:** the first works cable crossed the two Meridian rescue tethers, which drop vertically through the yard. The test caught it, and the cable was removed.

## Known limits
- **Collision is not yet live.** The solid set pieces have real collision data (`VISTA_SOLIDS`), but it takes effect only once the coordinator wires the hook below. Dressing stays visual-only by design.
- **Priority areas only.** Isles, Canopy, Rift and Divide rely on their existing bookmark compositions (stack, crowns, chimney, gateworks). The escarpment ring reads only as a partial arc from its bookmark.
- **No bake-time geology change.** The per-biome response is the shader's, keyed on depth; S2's baked stratum shading on cliffs is unchanged. The Divide service-ledge stripes are deliberate painted markings.
- **Gameplay views of the vistas.** The legacy Basin works is the only vista seen through the game itself; the rest were checked in the region viewer, because the simulation's world bounds still stop at the legacy area.
- **Rejected approach.** Flipping normals with `gl_FrontFacing` for two-sided blades darkened them (the winding convention is inverted), so it was dropped.

## R2: response to Sol R1 (`docs/build/reviews/A1-SOL-XHIGH-R1.md`)

**A1-R1-01 (blocking): solid-looking pieces now collide.**
- New Babylon-free `src/content/vistas.ts` holds every solid-looking piece as data:
  - arch voussoirs, hull plates, beams, markers, pipe saddles and lit lanterns are axis-aligned **blocks**, drawn as exactly that box;
  - ribs, keel, stringers, the beacon pole, boom chords, gantry legs, pipes and the ring are **tubes**, collided as one box per segment, grown by the radius (or by a collar's reach).
- `render/biomes/vistas.ts` draws those pieces only from that data (`drawSolidSet`), so art and collision cannot drift.
- `VISTA_SOLIDS` has 977 boxes in the `STRUCTURE_SOLIDS` shape.
- Shape changes that keep collision tight:
  - both hulls run along Z, so their ribs lie in constant-Z planes;
  - hull skin survives only where it runs near an axis, as slabs: 6 plates remain, and the 12.95 m² diagonal skin from R1 is gone;
  - the arch is now stepped, chamfered stone voussoirs, with the art inside each box;
  - the drop's coral mounds became open fan lace;
  - the Basin yard pipe became a 0.22 m conduit.
- Everything else is thin dressing, drawn to read as permeable: kelp, fans, bulbs, open lattice masts, thin lamps, cables and low debris.
- **Wiring hook for C3 (no `sim/*` edit here):** append `VISTA_SOLIDS.map(s => ({ id: s.id, min: s.bounds.min, max: s.bounds.max }))` to the indexed broad phase, next to `STRUCTURE_SOLIDS`. The composed region check context can add `VISTA_SOLIDS` to `solids` the same way.
- **Tests (`tests/vistas.test.ts`, fast tier, Babylon-free):**
  - every vertex of every solid set (fine and coarse) lies inside its own solids, within 2 cm;
  - no solid overlaps a scatter keep-out (`blockedBox`);
  - the authoritative `routeProblems` passes for every passage, and `firstAccessProblems` and `rescueProblems` pass, with the vista solids in context;
  - every S2 site's work pose stays more than 2 m from any solid, and every park pose more than the medium craft's radius plus 1 m;
  - the Basin yard stays more than 6 m from the legacy lanes and recovery tow, and more than 4 m from the station and dormitory parking and work poses;
  - adverse controls: a box planted on `route.basin.wreck_south` fails both `routeProblems` and `blockedBox`.
- **Placement fixes found by these tests:**
  - the ring moved 3 m east, off the escarpment route's keep-out;
  - the west works pipe crossed the gate hall's park pose, so it was rerouted south.

**A1-R1-02: vertical tethers are covered.** Keep-out lines are sampled every 3 m of 3D length, so headroom columns overlap down a vertical drop. Controls: the R1 midpoint `blocked(-228, -318, -78.25, 0, -78.25)` is now true. Scatter output is unchanged.

**A1-R1-03: sand and ring.**
- **Sand** (shader only; terrain bytes unchanged, 220/220):
  - near the camera on shallow level sand, small cross-ripples, three-scale grain and sparse grit flecks, all faded out by about 16–22 m;
  - patch contrast firmer close by;
  - firmer strata on steep ground;
  - the caustics' far-field average brightening lowered (0.06 → 0.035), so distance stops washing out;
  - no global pattern was added.
- **Ring:** turned to face the ledge's north approach (plane Z = −690), with a smaller top gap, lighter stone and lit inlays along its approach ridge. It now reads as a ring from `escarp`.

**R2 checks:**
- `npm test`: 738/738. Heavy: 16/16 under budget. Build passes. `bake-terrain --verify`: 220/220, and all 220 chunk entries equal the `a09968b` bake.
- **Shots:** RTX 3090, Chrome 156 GL-EGL, 1920×1080, in `~/.local/share/siltwake-evidence/A1/r2/`:
  - `r1-*` (the R1 candidate) against `r2-*` / `r2b-*` / `r2-sand-*` for `drop`, `reef`, `arch` (side view), `escarp`, `wrecks` and `works`;
  - `r*-sand-dropnear.png` points at open water, so ignore it; the drop bookmark's foreground is the close sand view.
- **GPU time per frame (timer query, static views):** about +0.2–0.4 ms over R1 (drop 2.40 → 2.63 ms, reef 3.22 → 3.79 ms). Traversals were not re-run: the host was saturated by other agents' tests, and R1's independent run already bounds the shader's cost.

## R2b: art inside a hugging envelope (coordinator, before the R2 review)

- **Rule:** art stays inside its collision, which may stand up to about 0.35 m off it. Bump-before-contact is allowed; swim-through is not.
- **Faceted pieces** (`VistaPiece` in `content/vistas.ts`):
  - the arch is a faceted rock arch again: a chain of 13 seven-sided frustums on a jittered centreline, with coral and amber on the crown's upward facets;
  - the hull keeps its curved surviving plates (back to a 0.42 survival fraction).
- **Slab covers:** each piece is collided by slabs across its dominant axis (0.6 m for arch rock, 0.4 m for plates). Each slab is the exact bounds of the facets inside it, computed by clipping polygons, so every box face touches the art.
- **Keel and stringers** are split into runs of 1 m or less.
- **Count:** `VISTA_SOLIDS` is now 1,973 boxes (arch 187, west hull 1,025, bow 495).
- **Enclosure test, both directions** (`tests/vistas.test.ts`):
  - samples over every solid-art triangle (spacing 0.25 m or less) lie inside the set's solids within 2 cm;
  - the centres of both thin-axis faces of every box lie inside a convex piece or within 0.35 m (+2 cm) of the art surface; that is 3,946 faces.
  - Measured by nearest-surface distance: an end slab of a skewed plate can miss the plate along the exact axis while sitting a few decimetres from it.
  - Mutation control: inflating the slabs by 0.5 m fails the test.
- **Checks:** `npm test` 738/738, heavy 16/16, build, and `bake-terrain --verify` 220/220.
- **Shots:** `r3-arch.png`, `r3-drop.png` and `r3-wrecks.png` in `~/.local/share/siltwake-evidence/A1/r2/`.
- **Traversal p99 not re-measured:** host load average was 8–13 on 6 vCPUs from other agents' suites.

## R3: response to Sol R2 (`docs/build/reviews/A1-SOL-XHIGH-R2.md`)

**A1-R2-01 (blocking): collision now hugs the art everywhere, not just at face centres.**
- **Cause:** axis-aligned boxes around rounded or slanted cross-sections bulged up to 1.55 m (arch) and 2.13 m (ring) past the art at their corners.
- **Shape change:** every solid-looking run is now a chain of **rounded-rectangle prisms** (`prism`/`beam` in `content/vistas.ts`); `VistaTube` is gone. That covers the arch rock, ring, ribs, keel, stringers, pipes, gantry legs, beacon pole and boom chords.
  - A prism's flat faces are square to the world axis most nearly perpendicular to its run. The arch, ring and ribs lie in constant-Z planes, so their Z faces are exactly flat.
  - Corner radii are at most 0.35 m on large prisms.
- **Slicing rules:**
  - slab width shrinks with slope, so a slanted slice's empty corner stays at about 0.12 m;
  - where an end cap spans more than 0.4 m along the slab axis, it is sliced at 0.25 m;
  - hull plates are each extruded straight along Z from their own rib, so they are planar and their slabs stay thin.
- **Changes made to fit:**
  - the bow section is now ribs and plates only: its fast-tapering, leaning ribs would need 3D-diagonal members;
  - three works pipes now run straight along an axis.
- **New test `tests/vistas-envelope.heavy.test.ts`** (heavy tier, about 15 s):
  - samples over every solid-art triangle (both LODs) lie inside the solids within 2 cm;
  - every box is sampled on a 0.25 m grid through its volume, faces, edges and corners, and each sample must be inside a convex piece or within 0.35 m (+2 cm) of the art surface;
  - the worst sample is 0.34 m (west hull);
  - mutation control: padding the slabs by 0.5 m fails the test.
- **Regression (fast tier):** the reviewer's diver poses beside the arch and ring report no contact through `corridorProblems` with `STRUCTURE_SOLIDS + VISTA_SOLIDS`.
- **Box count:** `VISTA_SOLIDS` is **5,271**, under the 6,000 line (5,195 after R4).

| Set | Boxes |
| --- | ---: |
| West hull | 2,622 |
| Bow | 864 |
| Ring | 492 |
| Arch | 582 |
| Boom | 429 |
| Pipes | 182 |
| Gantry | 64 |
| Markers | 36 |

  An oriented-box or capsule collider in C3 would cut this by roughly 10×, if broad-phase or narrow-phase cost becomes a concern.

**Checks:**
- `npm test`: 738/738. Heavy: 17/17, including the new envelope file. Build passes. `bake-terrain --verify`: 220/220.
- **Shots:** `r4-{drop,arch,wrecks,escarp,works}.png` in `~/.local/share/siltwake-evidence/A1/r2/`.
- **Traversal:** not re-run; the art changed only in the set pieces.

## R4: response to Sol R3 (`docs/build/reviews/A1-SOL-XHIGH-R3.md`)

**A1-R3-01 (blocking): fixed. The works pipes render where they collide.**
- **Cause:** the pipe set was anchored at X 1478, past the world's east edge (X ≤ 1472), so no chunk drew it, yet its 182 boxes were in the roster. One run also reached X 1515, and the south runs reached Z −1650, past the world's south edge (Z ≥ −1632).
- **Fix:**
  - the anchor is now (1440, −1610), inside the yard;
  - the yard has three runs south from the block's back to Z −1626, plus the north run beside the hatch;
  - the east lattice mast (dressing) moved from X 1474 to 1462.
- `VISTA_SOLIDS` is now **5,195** boxes.

**New invariant test (`tests/vistas.test.ts`, fast tier, through the real chunk path):**
- every solid set and every dressing part is owned by exactly one `s2.scatter` chunk of `worldLayout()`;
- every solid box lies inside `WORLD_ENVELOPE`;
- every set with solids draws art, and every set that draws art has solids;
- `vistaMesh()` over all chunks emits exactly the sum of every set's and dressing part's own vertices, at both LODs, so each is drawn exactly once.
- **Adverse controls:** the old anchor has no owning chunk, and restoring it in the compiled build fails the test.

**R4 checks:**
- `npm test`: 739/739. Heavy: 17/17, envelope included. Build passes. `bake-terrain --verify`: 220/220.
- **Shots:** `r5-works.png`, `r5-pipecheck.png` (the reviewer's diver pose; the pipe is now drawn there) and `r5-pipesouth.png`, in `~/.local/share/siltwake-evidence/A1/r2/`.
